pejorative

pih-JOR-uh-tiv · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pejorative is expressing contempt or disapproval, especially describing a word or phrase.

The term was once neutral but has since become pejorative.

Example

Linguists pointed out that the nickname, once affectionate, had gradually taken on a pejorative meaning.

A word that expresses contempt or disapproval, especially through how it's used over time, is exactly what pejorative describes.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

derogatory: A derogatory comment is one aimed at a person or group to lower them -- the word points at the remark and the act of insulting. Pejorative points at language itself: a term is pejorative when contempt is built into using it at all.

disparaging: A disparaging comment talks something down, dismissing it as small or second-rate, and it lives in one speaker's tone on one occasion. Pejorative belongs to the word itself: a pejorative term carries built-in contempt every time anyone uses it.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

complimentary: expressing praise or admiration

flattering: expressing praise, sometimes excessively

Where it sits · how insulting the wording is — negative → pejorative → abusive

negative vs. pejorative: A negative word is simply unfavorable; a pejorative one specifically expresses contempt or disapproval, often as an insult.

abusive vs. pejorative: Abusive goes further than pejorative: a pejorative term sneers its disapproval, while abusive language is an open verbal attack meant to wound.
